author: Adam Shinder
title: Revamped UAlbany women's basketball team kicks off preseason - NewsBreak
text:
By Adam Shinder ,
14 hours ago Head coach Colleen Mullen is seen during UAlbany women's basketball practice at Broadview Center on Tuesday, Sept. 23, 2025, in Albany, N.Y. (Lori Van Buren/Times Union) (Lori Van Buren/Times Union) ALBANY — The faces will be very different this season for University at Albany women’s basketball.
But the approach? Coach Colleen Mullen’s not changing that.
“It’s kind of a broken record with me: Defense, defense, defense,” Mullen said Tuesday following her team’s first official preseason practice.
Defense has been the Great Danes’ calling card in Mullen’s seven prior seasons at UAlbany, and it’s borne plenty of success — especially over the past four seasons. Mullen has led the program to four consecutive 20-win campaigns, never finishing worse than third in the America East Conference during that span.
But, coming off a season in which UAlbany went 26-7 and won the America East regular-season title before losing the conference tournament final to Vermont , Mullen’s got some rebuilding to do.
UAlbany heads into the 2025-26 season needing to replace six of its top seven scorers, including the entire top five. That group was led by 2024-25 America East Player of the Year Kayla Cooper , and included two more all-conference selections in Jessica Tomasetti and Kaci Donovan.
Mullen’s team for this season, which opens Nov. 4 at home against Marist, includes five returning players, five freshmen and two incoming transfers.
“It’s a new season. It’s a new team,” Mullen said. “Everybody has a new team coming back, so it’s a fresh start and I’m excited. We’re young, we’re unproven, we’re inexperienced, but that gives us a lot of opportunity to grow together and keep getting better every day.”
Sophomore guard Delanie Hill is the Great Danes’ only returning starter and the team’s top returning scorer, having averaged 3.4 points per game as a freshman.
She’s ready to use what she learned from players like Cooper and step into a leadership role.
“For my development, being the point guard on the floor and being the coach out there, learning to be a leader early is great,” Hill said. “Knowing the standards here and just teaching that has been a good experience.”
Junior guard Lara Langermann, who transferred to UAlbany after spending two seasons at New Mexico, said this Great Danes team came together quickly over the summer.
“It’s a new team, a lot of new players, but we got to know each other over the summer,” Langermann said. “There were a couple new players coming in (for the fall) that didn’t play with us in the summer, but we’re just really excited getting started with practice and preparing for our games.”
The Great Danes also benefited from a summer trip to Italy that included games and cultural experiences.
“Winning a game in Italy, competing and seeing that they can do it, that was critical,” Mullen said. “Now we are just working on taking those things from Italy, those 10 full practices that we had that were kind of a little treat before we actually had to start preseason … and I think it’s going to prove really valuable for our opening part (of the season).”
“It was so good,” Langermann said. “You got to spend every single day with somebody else, and then we got a great experience playing two games over there, which was great for getting a feel for how everybody plays, and how everybody feels in those game situations.”
Though UAlbany’s five returning players combined to average just 9.4 points last season and only one of them — senior center Gabriela Falcao — has spent more than one season on campus, Mullen said she’s looking at that group to set the tone for the team’s seven newcomers.
Hill and Falcao are joined as returning players by sophomore guards Martina Borrellas and Emma Harkonardottir, along with graduate student forward and Shenendehowa High School graduate Bella Stuart , who did not play in 2024-25 due to injury after transferring from New Hampshire.
“They’re used to winning,” Mullen said of her returning players. “They know what it takes.”
